{{Quote|I'm surprised you didn't recognize this other addition from the Covenant's own stores of Sith relics! The Gauntlet of Kressh the Younger&mdash;while I have it, no one may touch me without my consent!|Haazen, explaining the device on his mechanical arm|<ref name="Vindication3" />}}
The '''Gauntlet of Kressh the Younger''' was a [[Sith artifact/Legends|Sith artifact]] created during the time of the old [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] by the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Ludo Kressh]] to make his [[Elcho Kressh|son, Elcho]], invincible.

==Specifications==
[[File:KresshGauntletProtection.jpg|thumb|left|225px|The Gauntlet protecting [[Haazen]] from a lightsaber strike.]]
The Gauntlet was composed of five linked oval plates composed of an unknown black material, each capped with a red gem chased with gold. The middle three plates featured gold tassels hanging from the ends.<ref name="Vindication1">[[Knights of the Old Republic 32|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 32]]</ref>

Worn on the user's forearm, the Gauntlet had the power of preventing anything from touching the wearer without his or her consent, blasting aside anything that attempted to do so with a surge of Dark Side energy. Its protection was sufficient to defend the wearer from a lightsaber strike. In addition to providing protection, it also enabled the wearer to purposely direct such blasts towards chosen targets on a whim, without even needing to turn and face them.<ref name="Vindication3" />

However, the Gauntlet's protection was not absolute. As it only protected the wearer from things that didn't receive his consent, he could still be attacked by those who do. Also, one had to be wearing the Gauntlet for it to take full effect; simply holding it would not do.<ref name="Vindication3" />

==History==
An artifact of the Old [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]], the Gauntlet was created by Sith Lord Ludo Kressh for his son, Elcho. Kressh toiled endlessly upon perfecting the device so that it would render his son invulnerable from external harm.<ref name="Paragon" /><ref name="Knight Errant" />

By [[3963 BBY]], the artifact was retrieved by the [[Jedi Covenant]], a cabal of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] with an extremist anti-Sith attitude. It was taken from their stores by their leader, [[Haazen]]. Haazen was a failed Jedi turned [[Sith acolyte/Legends|Sith Acolyte]] who had worked with the Jedi seer, [[Krynda Draay]], to create the Jedi Covenant, deceiving her and all others in a long running scheme for control of the Jedi Order.<ref name="Vindication1" /> He concealed the Gauntlet in a large case in his office on the [[Draay Estate]], along with numerous other Sith artifacts, claiming that it was full of diagnostic equipment.<ref name="Vindication1" />

When [[Zayne Carrick]] was brought before the Covenant by [[Xamar]], masquerading as a dark sider in a bid to rescue Krynda Draay before the Jedi Council-aligned Knights attacked the estate, Haazen had the case and the Gauntlet brought to him. As the Jedi stormed the entrance to the estate, Haazen sent a blanket transmission to all Covenant-aligned Jedi, issuing the command word; [[Vindication]]. While the Covenant Jedi secured the Jedi Temple and the Sith artifacts stored there, Haazen brandished the Gauntlet and used a command device built into his prosthetic arm to take over the [[Vanjervalis Chain]] linking the Republic fleet computers, initiating an orbital strike on the Draay Estate entrance, killing many of the Council Jedi, including the turncoat Xamar.<ref name="Vindication1" />

[[File:Haazenpertylights.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Haazen activating the Gauntlet.]]

Donning the many Sith amulets and armor pieces in his case, and revealing [[Sabercane/Legends|his cane handle to be a concealed Sith lightsaber]], Haazen revealed his true allegiance to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]]. Protected from the initial explosions of the Republic bombardment by the Gauntlet, Haazen went on to reveal his entire scheme to those present. [[Lucien Draay]] twice attacked Haazen in defiance, only to be blasted back by the Gauntlet, the second blast destroying his lightsaber.<ref name="Vindication3" />

Haazen bestowed his Sith lightsaber upon Lucien, and declaring his intention to turn the Jedi into his Sith apprentice, Haazen went outside to receive the Sith artifacts being brought from the Jedi Temple. As he inspected the artifacts, Haazen witnessed the end of the duel between Lucien Draay and Zayne Carrick. When Carrick seemingly killed Draay and bowed before Haazen, the Sith believed that he had found a new apprentice. Allowing Carrick to touch him, Haazen lowered his guard, leaving Carrick with an opening to slice off Haazen's gauntlet hand; a grisly prosthesis.<ref name="Vindication4" />

As Haazen attacked Carrick with Force lightning, Carrick and his ally, [[Marn Hierogryph]], were sudden sent flying away by a massive surge of the Force. Lucien Draay revealed that he and Carrick had faked the duel to catch Haazen off-guard. Summoning Haazen's amputated prosthesis, Lucien used the Vanjervalis control device built in to cause the Republic fleet to fire on them.<ref name="Vindication4" />

Haazen was killed in the ensuing explosion, while Lucien Draay survived thanks to his possession of the Gauntlet. However, as he was only holding it rather than wearing it, its effects were only partial, and he was still left heavily scarred.<ref name="Vindication4" />

After that, the [[True Covenant]] built a [[Jedi Temple (Draay 2)|Temple]] on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Draay 2]] in order to hid the gauntlet. They built several traps to dissuade robbers or any explorers, including a statue of Lucien Draay, actually a [[Stone guardian/Legends|Stone guardian]]. The artifact itself was guarded by a swarm of [[sarl]]s. However the existence of the gauntlet was known and its location was mentioned in a [[Holocron/Legends|holocron]]. Millennia later, during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], it was known by the [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]] who coveted its power.<ref name="Lost Temple" />

In [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]] the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] worried that the gauntled would be discovered by [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] and used in favor of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatists]]. Jedi Knight [[B'ink Utrila]] and her Padawan, [[Rennax Omani]], following instructions from the holocron, led a [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone trooper]] [[Squad/Legends|squad]] in an expedition to Draay 2 in order to confirm the location of the Gauntlet, and prevent anyone to claim it. They found a pillar of sarls that was formed around the gauntlet, that started attacking them. Exposure to the gauntlet made them resistant to blaster fire and lightsabers. The pillar now unmade revealed the Sith artifact sought by the team hiding in the center of the room.<ref name="Lost Temple" />

Using the Force to push the creatures away from the artifact, Utrila cleared a path to it and leaped on. However, upon coming into contact with it she found herself overwhelmed by the powers of the dark side of the Force. Horrified by this, the Jedi Knight ordered immediate retreat, leaving the Gauntlet where it was as the sarls returned to their protective positions encasing it. She decided they should make camp and contact the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]] for further orders.<ref name="Lost Temple" />

During the night, they were attacked by a squad of [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]] commandos led by [[Pre Vizsla/Legends|Pre Vizsla]], who long knew about the Gauntlet and followed the group to find its exact location. The Jedi and clone squad engaged the Mandalorians in battle, during which Glitch intentionally reactivated the guardian droid, and eventually inserted a lightsaber in the wrong keyhole of the wall panel, activating a trap and causing the whole temple to collapse, along with himself.<ref name="Lost Temple" />

[[File:Gauntlet_3.jpg|thumb|Glitch disposing of the Gauntlet in a nearby river.]]
Both parties fled the ruining building. With the temple now destroyed, both parties departed the moon. Later, among the debris of the Jedi Temple, Glitch arose wearing the Gauntlet, undamaged due to its protective properties. Understanding that the artifact should not be used by anyone, the clone trooper locked it onto a stone and disposed of the Gauntlet by throwing it into the canyon river.<ref name="Lost Temple" />

==Behind the scenes==
It was revealed in ''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Paragon]]'' that the Gauntlet was built by [[Ludo Kressh]] himself for his son, making Kressh the Younger Ludo Kressh's son. It was later clarified that the identity of Kressh the Younger was Elcho Kressh in [[Knight Errant (novel)|''Knight Errant'']].
